sections.heading: C - New York Driver Manual Chapter Seven: Parallel parking
sections.markdown:
## C - New York Driver Manual Chapter Seven: Parallel parking

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
Parallel parking appears on every road test, alongside knowledge of illegal parking and the three no-series signs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
Cameras, sensors and self-parking aids assist backing but the driver stays ultimately responsible and must check behind before every reverse. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
Parkers pick a fitting same-side space, mirror-check and signal, stop about two feet beside the lead vehicle, both-shoulder-check for people and traffic, then creep back at full curb lock watching through the rear window with side and front glances. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A01
When front wheels oppose the lead bumper, drivers counter-steer while backing, clear the lead car, halt short of the rear car, then straighten and center with wheels at most one foot from the curb. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A01
Nearer-curb adjustment alternates forward and reverse with curb-then-straight steering, and road-side doors stay shut against interfering cyclists and traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A01
Hill parking sets the brake, selects Park or first gear, and angles wheels to the curb to block any traffic-bound roll. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=42]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A02
Space exits straighten the wheels, back toward the rear vehicle, and swing wheels away from the curb before merging [A02] [A01].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=43]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A02
Safe entry runs right-shoulder rear-window scan, interior-mirror watch, signal, side-mirror scan, left-shoulder slow roll clearing the front car, then left-shoulder merge when safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=43]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A02
Parking means stopped except briefly for goods or people, standing means stopped briefly for people only, and stopping means any halt however short. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=43]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A02
No-parking zones still allow brief goods-or-people loading, no-standing zones allow brief people loading with the driver aboard, and no-stopping zones allow halts only for devices, officers or collision avoidance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=43]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A02
Nothing may park, stop or stand within fifteen feet of a hydrant unless a licensed driver stays aboard, double-parked, on sidewalks or crosswalks, in intersections without permission, on rails, traffic-blocking beside work, within thirty feet of safety zones, or on bridges and in tunnels. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=43]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A02
Parking or standing is prohibited in front of a driveway, within twenty feet of an intersection crosswalk, within thirty feet of a traffic light, stop sign, or yield sign, within twenty feet of a fire station driveway or seventy-five feet on the opposite side, and along a cut or lowered curb, while parking is prohibited within fifty feet of a railroad crossing [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=43]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A03
Disability spaces demand DMV plates, a local permit or an out-of-state equivalent with the named holder aboard an operating vehicle, on streets and in larger shopping centers alike. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=44]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A03
Lying for disability plates is a misdemeanor with mandatory revocation plus fine, jail or both and a surcharge, while lying for a permit draws two-hundred-fifty to one-thousand-dollar civil penalties plus a surcharge, against applicant and certifying doctor alike. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=44]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A03
Form MV-664.1 seeks plates or permits, reserved spaces wear signs and possibly paint, and diagonal-striped access aisles stay empty for wheelchair and special-equipment access. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=44]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A03
Municipalities price street violations, while default shopping-center fines run fifty to seventy-five dollars first and seventy-five to one-hundred-fifty second within two years in one town, each plus a thirty-dollar surcharge. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=44]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A03
The chapter closes with review questions on curb distance, road-side doors, exit preparation, no-stopping meaning, passenger loading under no-series signs, and mid-block crosswalks. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=44]
